purpose:
To seek approval
from the Cabinet Member for Education and Skills for
Gloucestershire County Council to formally adopt the new
Gloucestershire Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education
2025–2030, following approval through the Agreed Syllabus
Conference process and in order to enable implementation by
Gloucestershire schools from September 2026.
content:
To seek approval
from the Cabinet Member for Education and Skills for
Gloucestershire County Council to formally adopt the new
Gloucestershire Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education
2025–2030, following approval through the Agreed Syllabus
Conference process and in order to enable implementation by
Gloucestershire schools from September 2026.
 

In coming to this decision I
have given due and full regard to the requirements of the public
sector equality duty contained in section 149 of the Equality Act
2010 (“the Act”) by reference to the law itself
and also the relevant Equality Impact Assessment, which was
prepared in accordance with the requirements of the
Act.  
 
Having fully considered
all the available information, I have decided to reject
the alternative options and take the recommended decision
to: 
 

Approve the formal adoption of the
Gloucestershire Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education
2025–2030 by Gloucestershire County
Council.  

 

Note that the Agreed Syllabus
Conference / SACRE process has considered the final draft syllabus
and that all four committees voted to adopt the new Agreed
Syllabus. 

 

Delegate authority to the Director
of Education to take all necessary operational steps to support
implementation, including communication with schools,
publication/access arrangements, and coordination of implementation
support through SACRE, the Religious Education adviser and existing
school communication routes.

purpose:
That the Director of Public Health



Approves the submission of a Stage 2 Full Application by
Gloucestershire County Council (GCC) to the Ministry of Defence
VALOUR Recognised Centre(s) Development Fund for up to £1
million of funding for the development of a Gloucestershire
Veterans and Forces Hub which will provide veterans and the wider
Armed Forces community with co-ordinated access to guidance and
support. GCC shall be identified in the application as the Lead
Organisation and Accountable Body for the programme and the
Gloucestershire charity, GL Communities, shall be identified as the
operational lead on the basis set out in this report.



Approves in the event that the above application is successful, the
carrying out of such further assurance checks as may be necessary
in relation to the potential liabilities arising from GCC acting as
Lead Organisation and Accountable Body and before determining
whether to enter into:

a final funding agreement with the Armed Forces Covenant Trust;
and

a separate partnership agreement with GL Communities under which GL
Communities shall act as the operational lead.


A separate decision will be taken to determine whether the Council
should enter into the two agreements referred to above once the
requisite assurance checks have been completed.

purpose:
To seek Cabinet approval on the approach to be
taken in respect of the development of the M5 Junction 9
(Ashchurch) and A46 Transport Scheme.
content:
Cllr Julian Tooke sought Cabinet approval
on the approach to be taken in respect of the
development of the M5 Junction 9 (Ashchurch) and A46 Transport
Scheme.
 
 
Having considered all of the information,
Cabinet noted the report and RESOLVED to:
 
Delegate authority to the
Executive Director of Economy, Environment and Infrastructure in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Business, Economic
Development, Planning & Infrastructure to:
 

1.             
Award without further competition a call-off
contract for the supply of professional Highways Traffic and
Transport services during the period 1 August 2026 to 31st March
2027 under Lot 5 of the Eastern Shires Purchasing Organisation
(ESPO) Consultancy Services (664-25) framework agreement to the
preferred tender, namely AtkinsRealis, in accordance with the
framework’s direct award criteria. The provision of the above
services will enable consultancy work to continue on the
council’s above-mentioned Strategic Outline Case (SOC) and
Outline Business Case (OBC) relating to the M5 Junction 9 and A46
(Ashchurch) Transport Scheme.
 

2.             
Continue work on the council’s Strategic
Outline Case (SOC) and Outline Business Case (OBC) relating to the
M5 Junction 9 and A46 (Ashchurch) Transport Scheme, between 1
August 2026 and 31 October 2026, capping the cost of such work at
£534k, funded from existing resources - previously approved
CIL contributions.
 

3.             
Increase the scheme approvals by £360k to
ensure the overall scheme approvals match the proposed spend to
October 2026.
 

4.             
A further report is required in October 2026 to
clarify government’s commitment to the scheme, which is
required to release further funding and scheme approvals. The
Department for Transport (DfT) was expected to make an announcement
regarding the future of the M5 J9 and A46 (Ashchurch) Transport
Scheme in the Large Local Majors/Major Road Network programme, in
early summer (July 2026). However, with the recent changes in
parliament involving a new Prime Minister, an announcement has been
made by Government that it is unlikely that any new funding
decisions will now occur before September.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the approach for the development of the M5 Junction 9 (Ashchurch) and A46 Transport Scheme.

purpose:
To seek delegated authority to procure
and award a contract for the provision of a domestic abuse/healthy
relationship support service for young people in
Gloucestershire
content:
To seek delegated authority to procure
and award a contract for the provision of a domestic abuse/healthy
relationship support service for young people in
Gloucestershire
 

Cllr Paul Hodgkinson sought delegated authority to procure and award a contract for the
provision of a domestic abuse/healthy relationship support service
for young people in Gloucestershire.
 
Having considered all of the information,
Cabinet noted the report and

RESOLVED to:
 
Delegate authority to the
Director of Public Health, in consultation with the Cabinet Member
for Public Health, Communities and Fire to:


1.             
Conduct a competitive procurement process in respect
of a contract for the supply of the council’s young
persons’ healthy relationship service, which includes
domestic abuse support for children and young people victims who
are in safe accommodation (see paragraph 20). The proposed contract
shall continue for an initial period of two years (commencing 1
April 2027) and include options to extend its term for a further
period of two years on its second and fourth anniversaries (i.e.,
two + two + two years).
 
2. Award the above contract to
the preferred tenderer.

3. Determine whether to exercise
each of the above contract extension options subject to
satisfactory performance, continued service need and confirmation
of continued availability of funding from the council’s
domestic abuse and education budgets, and the Domestic Abuse (DA)
Duty Funding/domestic abuse grant underspend (see paragraph
20).

4. Approve the allocation of
£270,000 (i.e. £45,000 per year) from the Domestic
Abuse (DA) Duty Funding/domestic abuse grant underspend (see
paragraph 20) to be included within the overall budget for part
funding the contract described in Recommendation 1 above during its
six-year term (that is, if both the above extension options are
exercised) which will include the provision of specific domestic
abuse support for children and
young people victims who are in
safe accommodation within the recommissioned service (see paragraph
20).

5. Enter into an initial two-year
Funding Agreement with the OPCC under which the council will
receive a funding transfer of up to £60,000 per annum during
its term from Gloucestershire OPCC to fund one full time Children
and Young Person Independent Domestic Violence Advisor (CHIDVA) in
the recommissioned service proposed in Recommendation 1 above (on
the basis described in the Resource Implications section below)
during the period 1 April 2027 until 31 March 2029.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to delegate authority to procure and award a contract for a domestic abuse/healthy relationship support service for young people in Gloucestershire.

(under Lot E). The proposed call-off contract shall continue for an

12 month extension options each commencing on the relevant contract
anniversary (i.e., 2+1+1 years).
 

3.    
Delegate authority to the Director of Public Health,
in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Public Health,
Communities and Fire to determine whether to exercise any or all of
the extension options described in Recommendations 2(b), 2(c), and
2(d) based on the availability of funding, satisfactory provider
performance and continued service need.
 

4.    
Approve the allocation of between £189,924 and
£211,026 from the DA Duty Funding per year for the purpose of
funding housing support and housing management costs within the
Places of Safety scheme (described in Recommendation 5 and
paragraph 7 below) during the period 1 November 2026 – 30
October 2030.
 

5.    
Delegate authority to the Public Health Manager for
Domestic Abuse to identify the actual sum to be allocated based on
the number of units of dispersed domestic abuse safe accommodation
that are required by the Gloucestershire Housing Partnership (which
includes Gloucestershire County Council as a member).
 

6.   
Approve the annual transfer of the DA Duty funding
described in Recommendation 4 during the period 1 November 2026 to
30 October 2030 to whichever local authority holds the contract for
the provision of housing support and management services with the
contracted provider of such services under the Places of Safety
scheme (currently Gloucester City Council). For the avoidance of
doubt, if the said contract is terminated before 30 October 2030
(as the result of Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) – see
paragraph 9 of the Background section of this report) no further
payments shall be made under this recommendation after the
termination date of the contract, in which case alternative uses
for the funding shall be considered and presented for approval
through the appropriate governance decision making
route.
 

7.    
Approve the council entering into a Grant Agreement
with Gloucester City Council in respect of the DA Duty funding
described in Recommendations 4 to 6 above.
 

8.    
Approve a change to Decision 5(a) contained in the
Cabinet report dated 24 July 2024 by:
 
Delegate authority to the Director of Public Health in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Public Health, Communities
and Fire to allocate from the above DA Duty Funding a maximum of
£275,000 (i.e. £95,000 per year) over a period of three
years to Gloucester City Council as the host local authority for
the Housing Partnership Team (which acts on behalf of the District
and County Councils, the Gloucestershire Office of the Police and
Crime Commissioner (OPCC) and the Gloucestershire Integrated Care
Board (ICB)) for the purpose of funding the provision of domestic
abuse support in a pilot Respite Rooms scheme). The final value of
this allocation will be determined by the Director of Public
Health, based on the agreed design of the Respite Rooms scheme,
including staffing capacity and specialist support provision. (See
paragraph 12 for further details).
 

9.    
Approve the council to enter into a Grant Agreement
with Gloucester City Council in respect of the DA Duty Funding set
out in Recommendation 8 above.
 

10.Delegate authority to the
Executive Director of Children’s Services to allocate a total
of £200,000 from the DA Duty Funding for the purpose of
funding the cost of procuring and awarding as many call-off
contracts for the provision of wellbeing and recovery support for
children and young people in need of domestic abuse safe
accommodation under the council’s Access to Resources (A2R)
Framework during the period 1 September 2027 – 31 August
2028. Authority to procure and award the said call-off contracts
was delegated by Cabinet to the Executive Director for
Children’s Services on 10 November 2021.
 
 
11.
Approve the allocation of an estimated total of £524,913
(£326,718 DA Duty Funding and £198,195 domestic abuse
grant underspend) for the purpose of funding the cost of the
following roles and the council’s corporate support costs
during the period 1 July 2026 – 30 June 2028:

(a)
50% of the annual salary of the council’s Public Health
Manager for domestic abuse employed by the council. The remaining
50% will continue to be funded from the Public Health and
communities staffing budget;
 
(b)
50% of the annual salary and on-costs of the jointly funded
Domestic Abuse and Violence Against Women and Girls (DA and VAWG)
Policy and Strategy Lead employed by Gloucestershire Office of the
Police and Crime Commissioner (OPCC). The remaining 50% will
continue to be funded the OPCC;

(c)
60% of the annual salary and on-costs of the jointly funded
Consultation Coordinator employed by the OPCC (in the OPCC’s
DA and VAWG Team) The remaining 40% will continue to be funded the
OPCC,

(d)
50% of the annual salary and on-costs of the jointly funded DA and
VAWG Research Officer employed by the OPCC. The remaining 50% will
continue to be funded the OPCC.

(e)
100% of the salary of the council’s Senior Public Health
Officer for domestic abuse (previously funded by the
council’s Public Health and Communities staffing budget);
and

(f) A
contribution of 4.4% of the value of the total DA Duty Funding
allocation per annum towards the council’s overheads and
corporate costs associated with administering the DA Duty
Funding.

12.
Delegate authority to the Director of Public Health, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Public Health, Communities
and Fire to:


a) Allocate up to £270,000 to fund the cost of
the council providing statutory partners within the Domestic Abuse
Local Partnership Board (LPB) (i.e. the partners identified within
Annex 2 of the Gloucestershire Tackling Domestic Abuse Strategy)
with opportunities to request funding to support their approach to
supporting victims in domestic abuse safe accommodation.

b) Make decisions on proposals from the LPB in
relation the funding requests and, if approved, to authorise the
transfer of an appropriate proportion of the funding described in
Recommendation 11(a) to the relevant statutory
organisation.

 

13. Approve the allocation of £744,717 of
historic underspend by Gloucestershire County Council from the
domestic abuse grant to fill any gaps in funding towards the cost
of the projects/contracts for support in safe accommodation set out
in Annex 2 in the event that the council does not receive DA Duty
Funding or receives lower DA Duty Funding after 2028/29 than the
value for 2028/29 as set out in the resource implication section of
this report.


14. Approve a change in the source of funding for
the projects/contracts approved by cabinet in March 2023, July 2024
and March 2025, and an officer decision dated February 2023
described in Annex 3 that were funded from historic domestic abuse
grant underspend or the council’s domestic abuse budget. The
funding for these projects will now instead be sourced from DA Duty
Funding given that recurrent DA Duty funding became available from
April 2026, hence it was not available when the original decisions
were made. These projects meet the purpose of the DA Duty Funding
as specified in the statutory support in safe accommodation
guidance issued by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local
Government.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to allocate funding for domestic abuse support in safe accommodation for the period July 2026 – June 2032.

for the provision of cleaning and caretaking services across

content:
To seek Cabinet
approval to modify the council’s existing call-off contracts
for the provision of cleaning and caretaking services across
participating schools and the council’s corporate estate
under its framework agreement of the same name by extending their
terms for a period of 6 months (from 1 August 2027) for the purpose
of allowing sufficient time to procure a replacement contract for
these services that reflects the council’s modified
requirements arising from the forthcoming Local Government
Reorganisation process
 
To also seek
delegated authority to procure a replacement Cleaning and
Caretaking Framework Agreement and call-off contracts under it that
will commence following the expiry of the above proposed
extension.
 

Cllr Colin Hay sought Cabinet approval to modify
the council’s existing call-off contracts for the provision
of cleaning and caretaking services across participating schools
and the council’s corporate estate under its framework
agreement of the same name by extending their terms for a period of
6 months (from 1 August 2027) for the purpose of allowing
sufficient time to procure a replacement contract for these
services that reflects the council’s modified requirements
arising from the forthcoming Local Government Reorganisation
process

He also sought delegated authority to procure a
replacement Cleaning and Caretaking Framework Agreement and
call-off contracts under it that will commence following the expiry
of the above proposed extension.
 
Having considered all of the information,
Cabinet noted the report and RESOLVED to:
 
 

1.             
Approve a six-month extension (commencing 1 August
2027) to the term of the Council’s call-off contract for all
properties listed in Appendix 1 for the provision of cleaning and
caretaking services at the Council’s 111 corporate properties
under the Council’s framework for the provision of such
services, together with the related call-off contracts currently in
place for the 75 participating schools. The extension shall be
implemented by means of a contract modification to each call-off
contract. Participating schools will have the option to extend
their contracts and, where they elect to do so, will be required to
enter into new order forms for the six-month extension
period.
 

2.             
Delegate authority to the Deputy Chief Executive and
Executive Director of Corporate Resources (S151 Officer), in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Finance, Assets and
Transformation, to:
 

a)    
conduct a competitive procurement process in respect
of a four-year multi-supplier Framework Agreement, commencing 1
February 2028, for the supply of cleaning and caretaking services
for:
 
(i)
the Council’s corporate estate currently comprising
approximately 111 properties (noting that responsibility for that
estate may transfer to successor authority/authorities because of
the forthcoming Local Government Reorganisation (LGR)
process;
(ii) participating schools
within Gloucestershire (noting that approximately 75 schools have
expressed an interest in joining the proposed new
framework:
 
(iii) external public sector
partners, listed in paragraph 5 of the Background section of this
report;
The Framework Agreement will be
divided into the following geographical Lots:
Lot 1 – Tewkesbury and
North Cotswolds
Lot 2 – South
Cotswolds
Lot 3 – Forest of
Dean
Lot 4 –
Gloucester
Lot 5 –
Cheltenham
Lot 6 – Stroud
If, however, it becomes necessary
to revise the above lots because of the LGR process, a separate
decision through the appropriate governance decision making route
shall be sought at the relevant time to authorise such
revision.
b) appoint each preferred
tenderer to the relevant Lot or Lots under the above Framework
Agreement. The maximum number of Lots to which any single tenderer
may be appointed is five;
c) award up to six call-off
contracts (i.e., one call-off contract per Lot if all six Lots are
awarded to different tenderers) under this Framework Agreement, to
the suppliers appointed to supply cleaning and caretaking services
at the council’s corporate estate properties, while noting
that participating schools and external public sector partners will
award and fund their own call-off contracts under the Framework
Agreement if they choose to use it. Where any individual call-off
contract award by the Council is anticipated to exceed
£500,000 in value, a separate Cabinet or Cabinet Member key
decision will be sought at the relevant time;
Each of the call-off contracts
awarded by the council under the above Framework Agreement shall
continue for a period of six years and six months and shall include
break/ termination provisions exercisable by the council on each
anniversary of the relevant call-off contract from the second
anniversary onwards. The call-off contracts awarded by schools and
external public sector partners shall also continue for the same
period and include the same break/termination options exercisable
by the relevant schools and external public sector
partners;
d) Exercise any of the
council’s break/termination provisions under the relevant
authority’s call-off contracts awarded under the Framework
Agreement if there is a material default, or detrimental change in
the financial standing and/or credit rating.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to extend existing contracts for cleaning and caretaking services in schools and council properties to reflect modified requirements due to Local Government Reorganisation.

purpose:
To approve the
proposed policy for the Council to charge residents for recycling
excess Do-It-Yourself (DIY) waste above the free allowance at
Household Recycling Centres (HRCs).
content:
To approve the
proposed policy for the Council to charge residents for recycling
excess Do-It-Yourself (DIY) waste above the free allowance at
Household Recycling Centres (HRCs).


Cllr Ashley Bowkett
sought Cabinet approval for the proposed policy for
the Council to charge residents for recycling excess Do-It-Yourself
(DIY) waste above the free allowance at Household Recycling Centres
(HRCs).
 
 
Having considered all of the information,
Cabinet noted the report and RESOLVED to:
 
 
1. Approve the adoption of the
DIY Waste Charging Policy set out in Appendix 1 to this report in
relation to excess DIY waste brought by residents above the free
allowance for recycling and disposal at the council’s five
Household Recycling Centres.

2. Delegate authority to the
Executive Director of Economy, Environment and Infrastructure in
consultation with the Cabinet member for Nature, Climate and Waste
Reduction to:

2.1 Implement the above DIY Waste
Charging Policy at all five HRCs in Gloucestershire;
 
2.2 conduct a search and
assessment process under Lots 1-3 of the Crown Commercial Services
Framework RM1557 (G-Cloud 13) to identify the preferred tenderer
that best meets the council’s budget and specification
requirements in respect of a call-off contract for the supply and
ongoing support / maintenance of an online customer booking and
payment system to facilitate the implementation of the above DIY
Waste Charging Policy. The call-off contract shall continue for a
period of 3 years commencing September 2026 and include an option
to extend its term for a further period of 12 months.
 
 
2.3 Award the above call-off
contract to the preferred tenderer.

2.4 Determine whether to exercise
the above 12-month extension option on the expiry of the initial 3
year term subject to satisfactory supplier performance and
continued service need.

3. Modify the council’s
existing Household Recycling Centre Service contract with Ubico Ltd
(a waste services company that is owned and controlled by
Gloucestershire County Council and seven other local authorities)
for the purpose of making provision for any additional Ubico staff
that may become necessary in order to implement the above DIY Waste
Charging Policy at each of the five HRCs.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to charge residents for recycling excess DIY waste above the free allowance at Household Recycling Centres.

purpose:

content:
To seek Individual
Cabinet Member approval to expand the council’s existing
Fostering Capital Support Scheme to include the purchase of
vehicles during the period April 2026 – March 2027 for the
purpose of enabling foster carers and special guardians to access
suitable vehicles to allow them to transport an increased number of
children, including larger sibling groups, safely
 

In coming to this decision I
have given due and full regard to the requirements of the public
sector equality duty contained in section 149 of the Equality Act
2010 (“the Act”) by reference to the law
itself and also the relevant Equality Impact Assessment, which
was prepared in accordance with the requirements of the
Act.  
 
Having fully considered
all the available information, I have decided to reject
the alternative options and take the recommended decision
to: 
 

Approve an expansion of the
council’s existing Fostering Capital Scheme to permit funding
to be directed towards the purchase, during the period April 2026
– March 2027, of suitable vehicles by foster carers and
special guardians to allow them to safely transport additional
children coming into their care, or for the larger sibling groups
already in their care. 


Delegate authority to the Assistant
Director Corporate Parenting to consider and, where appropriate,
approve individual applications made by foster carers or special
guardians for vehicle purchase during the period April 2026 –
March 2027 and, to release funding to successful applicants,
provided they satisfy all the following eligibility criteria:


The applicant must be an approved
Gloucestershire Foster Carer (including Kinship Carers) or an
approved Special Guardian, where the Special Guardianship Order
application was supported by Gloucestershire County Council
Children’s Services. 


The applicant must be caring for
a child from Gloucestershire. 


The applicant must have a minimum
of one year’s fostering or caring
experience.  


The applicant
must demonstrate a strong record of fostering/caring
experience and commitment, evidenced through successful
annual reviews.  


The applicant must be
offering additional placements and show a clear
commitment to sustaining this provision for Gloucestershire,
including supporting the stability of children already in their
care where increased capacity enables them to remain within their
existing foster home. 

 
 
For the reasons set
out in the report.

integrated pathways across education, health and care, and
improving outcomes for children and families through:

originally.

paragraph 4 within the background section of this report. As well
as delegate authority to the Executive Director of Children’s
Services, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Education and

including making any necessary operational decisions required to
give effect to Recommendation 1, within the overall funding
envelope and purposes set out in this report.

Note: Cabinet originally approved £676,000 in February 2026;

this report. As well as delegate authority to the Executive
Director of Children’s Services, in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Education and Skills, to implement and manage
the agreed programme of spend, including making any necessary

Note: Cabinet originally approved £1,030,600 in February

·      
Children with Additional Needs funding of £1,788,700 for the

this report. As well as delegate authority to the Executive
Director of Children’s Services, in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Education and Skills, to implement and manage
the agreed programme of spend, including making any necessary
operational decisions required to give effect to Recommendation 1,
within the overall funding envelope and purposes set out in this
report.

Note: this is new allocated funding, hence it was not the subject
of an earlier Cabinet decision
·      
Local authority facilitated Early Years Foundation Stage profile
assessment support - £32,800 (new allocated funding)

Note: this is new allocated funding, hence it was not the subject
of an earlier Cabinet decision.
 

2.   
Delegate authority to the Executive Director of Children’s
Services to:
a.   
Implement the above programme of spend, including determining and
approving the detailed delivery arrangements required to deliver
the Best Start in Life programme ensuring alignment with the
Council’s wider education, early years and school readiness
priorities;
b.   
Take all necessary operational and financial decisions to ensure
that the programme is delivered in accordance with the Department
for Education’s grant conditions, the Memorandum of
Understanding and the nationally prescribed programme framework
including those relating to education improvement, early years
quality, and integrated multi-agency delivery
c.    
Make any minor amendments to the allocation of funding between
approved budget headings, where required for effective programme
delivery, provided that such amendments remain within the overall
approved grant allocation.
d.   
Develop, approve and publish a Best Start in Life local delivery
plan and allocate grant funding to improve early outcomes, reduce

decision_maker: Cabinet Member - Nature, Climate & Waste Reduction
purpose:
To seek approval to revise the procurement
route that was approved under an individual cabinet member decision
3rd October 2025
content:
In coming to this decision I have given due
and full regard to the requirements of the public sector equality
duty contained in section 149 of the Equality Act 2010 (“the
Act”) by reference to the law itself.
 
Having fully considered all the
available information, I have decided to reject the alternative
options and take the recommended decision to:
 
1.   
Ratify a decision taken by Executive Director for
Economy, Environment and Infrastructure to conduct a competitive
procurement process in respect of a four-year, multi-supplier
framework agreement for the supply, delivery and installation
of:
 
a)   
static waste compaction equipment for use at county
council operated Household Recycling Centres, including an
associated three-monthly maintenance service for a 5-year period
(Lot 1); and
b)   
skips for use with the static waste compaction
equipment at county council operated Household Recycling Centres
(Lot 2).
 
This recommendation, if
approved, replaces the decision taken by Lead Cabinet Member for
Nature, Climate and Waste Reduction on 3rd October 2025 to procure
a contract with a single provider for the delivery, installation
and ongoing servicing and refurbishment of static waste compaction
equipment at Hempsted Household
Recycling Centre, given that subsequent development of the
procurement strategy identified that a framework agreement with two
lots would provide a more appropriate and efficient mechanism for
meeting operational needs across the HRC network.
 
2.   
Ratify a decision by Executive Director for Economy,
Environment and Infrastructure, following the conclusion of the
above procurement process, to:
 
a)   
Appoint the preferred tenderer, namely Bergmann
Direct Ltd, as the sole supplier of static waste compaction
equipment and services under Lot 1 of the above
framework;
b)   
Appoint the preferred tenderer, namely Skip Units
Ltd, as the sole supplier of skips for use with the static waste
compaction equipment and services under Lot 2 of the above
framework.
 
3.   
Approve the award of the following call-off
contracts under the above framework agreement:
 
a)   
A call-off contract award to Bergmann Direct Ltd
under Lot 1 of the above framework relating to the supply, delivery
and installation of six static compactors and a three-monthly
maintenance service plan over a 5-year period at Hempsted Household Recycling centre.
b)   
A call-off contract award to Skip Units Ltd under
Lot 2 of the above framework relating to the supply, delivery and
installation of nine skips for use with the static waste compaction
equipment at Hempsted Recycling
Centre.
 
Delegate authority
to the Executive Director of Economy, Environment &
Infrastructure in consultation with the said Cabinet Member to
progress the vital repair works at Hempsted Household Recycling centre through to
completion. This will include the closure of Hempsted Household Recycling Centre to the public
for approximately three months commencing in August 2026, this is
now considered the optimal time with, regards to weather and
resident site usage, to undertake vital works. This recommendation,
if approved, replaces the cabinet member decision dated 3 October
2025 to close Hempsted for vital works
in January 2026
topline: The Cabinet Member for Nature, Climate & Waste Reduction has decided to ratify a competitive procurement process for waste compaction equipment and skips at Household Recycling Centres.

Cllr Colin Hay
reported on the delivery of the Council
Strategy during Quarter 4 2025/26, including the current
performance and risk position. Cabinet was asked to consider the
Council's revenue outturn expenditure for 2025/26, agree
recommendations for reserve transfers; and approve additions and
funding changes to the Capital Programme, noting the 2025/26 final
capital outturn.
 
 
 
Having considered all of the
information, Cabinet noted the report and

RESOLVED to:
 
 

1.    
Note this report of the delivery of the Council
Strategy action plan and the    current performance and risk position.
To do this, the following are provided:


·      
Financial Overview

·      
Overview of Performance

·      
Delivery of Council Strategy

·      
Performance Scorecard

·      
Risk Scorecard
 

2.    
Note the 2025/26 revenue budget underspend of
£7.642 million.
 

3.    
Approves the transfer of £7.642 million to the
following reserves:


a)   
£1.070 million to the Local Government
Reorganisation Reserve, to achieve a balance of £11.7 million
which has previously been identified as GCC’s minimum share
of transition costs.


b)   
The balance of the underspend, £6.572 million,
is transferred to the Risk and Opportunities Reserve, to be held
pending further Cabinet review of any emerging risks or
opportunities in the current financial year. The Council’s
most significant financial risk is the potential requirement to
fund a 10% contribution to the residual Dedicated Schools Grant
deficit following the end of the statutory override in April 2028.
The County Council’s position remains that Central Government
should fund DSG deficits in full.
 
 

4.    
Approve other technical reserve movements for
2025/26 as set out in Annex 2.


5.    
Note in section B the delivery of £25.656
million of savings against a target of £26.434 million in

Approve the changes to capital programme of
transfers (virements) and funding increases, as detailed in
paragraph 86.

Note in section G the capital outturn position for

£150.568 million, giving an in-year slippage of £8.241
million.

Note in section H the Council’s performance
against the Prudential Indicators for 2025/26.

services.

review, termination, or expiry in accordance with their
terms.

for the provision of adult learning services.
content:
Cllr Linda Cohen, sought Cabinet delegated authority to enter into a funding agreement with the
Department for Education (DfE) for the purpose of funding the
delivery of Tailored Learning and the Adult Skills Programme during
the 2026-2027 academic year and then to procure and award a number

services.

Executive Director of Economy, Environment and
Infrastructure, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for

agreement with the Department for Education (DfE) under which the

2026–2027 academic year.

competitive open procurement under the Procurement Act 2023,

Steps provision
o Employability provision
o Adults

provision

training needs).

contracts to the relevant preferred tenderer(s), with each contract

Cllr Julian Tooke sought Cabinet adoption of

Having considered all of the information,

RESOLVED to:
 
A) Agree to adopt

Executive Director for Economy, Environment and Infrastructure, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Business, Economic

purpose:
To provide an annual update of the progress
with the Gloucestershire Climate Change report, and seek approval
for the report.
content:
Cllr Martin Horwood provided the
annual update of the Council’s progress with its
Gloucestershire Climate Change report and sought approval for the
report and recommendations on net zero commitments.
 
 
Having considered all of the
information, Cabinet noted the report and
 
RESOLVED to:
 
1. Acknowledge GCC commitment to
a target of achieving net zero for its own corporate emissions
(Scope 1) by 2030.

2. Confirm GCC continuation of
purchasing electricity with Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin
(REGO) for bought-in electricity (Scope 2) to maintain zero
emissions.
 
3. Acknowledge GCC commitment to
a target of achieving net zero for supplier and contractor
emissions (Scope 3) by 2050, working with suppliers and contractors
to monitor, report and take action to reduce their greenhouse gas
emissions. It commits to help and support for Small and Medium
Enterprises (SMEs), through the Growth Hub (a free to use business
advisory service)https://www.thegrowthhub.biz/business-support/,
which will continue engagement with smaller businesses on climate
action.
 
4. For pensions, notes that under
the Gloucestershire Pension Fund a net zero target of 2045 has been
set and asks the Gloucestershire Pension Fund to reconsider
complete disinvestment from all fossil fuels in the
meantime.
 
5. Delegate authority to EE&I
Director, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Nature,
Climate and Waste Reduction, the Head of Paid Service, the Section
151 Officer and Monitoring Officer, to develop plans to incentivise
modal shift and travel reduction by GCC employees and contractors,
in line with the policy objectives of the Gloucestershire Local
Transport Plan.

6. Note the publication of the
sixth Annual Climate Change report
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve ambitious targets for achieving net zero emissions by 2030 and 2050 for corporate and supplier emissions, respectively.

for the supply of the central funding application and assessment
service outlined in this report.
 
Having considered all of the
information, Cabinet noted the report and
 
RESOLVED to:
 
That subject to receipt of the
Crisis and Resilience Fund grant determination letter and funding
to the indicative amount of £5,700,000 per year for the
period 1st April 2026 to 31st March 2029, Cabinet:


1.             
Approve the acceptance by Gloucestershire County
Council (GCC) of the Crisis and Resilience Fund 2026–2029
Grant from the Department for Work and Pensions.


2.             
Delegate authority to the Executive Director of
Children’s Services in consultation with the Cabinet Member
for Children’s Safeguarding and Care to allocate Crisis and
Resilience Fund grant funding to the following initiatives during
the period 1st April 2026 to 31st March 2029 as described in the
Crisis and Resilience Fund guidance.

 

a) Allocate £1,900,000 (33%) annually towards
the delivery of the crisis element of the Crisis and Resilience
Fund, under which, Gloucestershire County Council will deliver a
central funding application and assessment service;
 

b) Allocate £570,000 (10%) annually towards
administration costs incurred by Gloucestershire County Council in
providing local coordination for the Crisis and Resilience Fund as
described in this report;
 

c) Allocate £2,760,000 (48%) annually towards
the delivery of the resilience element of the Crisis and Resilience
Fund as described in this paper. This will be delivered, through UK
Subsidy Control Regime compliant grants for community-based
organisations;
 

d) Allocate £470,000 (8%) annually towards the
delivery of the community coordination element of the Crisis and
Resilience Fund objectives as described in this paper. This will be
delivered through UK Subsidy Control Regime compliant grants to
community-based organisations
 
If the value of any of the grants
to be awarded under this Recommendation 2 exceeds £500,000, a
separate key decision will be sought from Cabinet or (as
appropriate) an individual Cabinet Member at the relevant time to
authorise the award of such grants.
 
 
 

3.

content:
To confirm the approach towards

and Community 20s programme and to seek approval for the
implementation of this programme.

Cllr Roger Whyborn and Cllr Paul
Hodgkinson sought Cabinet approval to confirm the approach towards
prioritisation, engagement, and decision making for the Safer Roads
and Community 20s programme and to seek approval for the
implementation of this programme.
 
 
Having considered all of the
information, Cabinet noted the report and
 
RESOLVED to:
 
1. Endorse the approach to prioritisation,
communications and engagement and decision making in relation to
the Safer Roads and Community 20s programme as set out in this
report;

2. Agree the Safer Roads and Community 20s
outline delivery programme for 2026/27 and the provisional
programme for 2027/28 in Appendix A, Appendix B and Appendix
C.

3. Delegate authority to the Director of
Traffic and Highways and the Director of Public Health, in
consultation with the Cabinet Members for Sustainable Transport and
Strategic Highways and for Public Health, Communities and Fire and
the Director of Public Health to:

(a) finalise the programme for the financial
year 2026/27 and continue to develop the programme for 2027/28 and
future years;

(b) implement delivery of the finalised
programme for Safer Roads and Community 20s in the four phases as
set out in the body of the report;

(c) regularly review and update the programme
to reflect the outcome of public engagements, funding
considerations, road safety issues and deliverability;

(d) Where possible streamline the Traffic
Regulation Order process to enable the most efficient delivery of
the programme; and

(e) update the council’s road safety
audit protocols to support the safe and efficient delivery of the
programme.

that has been awarded to the council by the Department for

re-procure existing bus services and home to school transport

and 31 August 2027.

purpose:
To seek Cabinet approval to establish a joint
programme with Gloucestershire’s District Councils to deliver
Local Government Reorganisation across Gloucestershire, supported
by a pooled budget with Gloucestershire County Council acting as
the Accountable Body.
content:
Cllr Lisa Spivey sought Cabinet
approval to establish a joint programme with
Gloucestershire’s District Councils to deliver Local
Government Reorganisation across Gloucestershire, supported by a
pooled budget with Gloucestershire County Council acting as the
Accountable Body.
 
 
Having considered all of the
information, Cabinet noted the report and
 
RESOLVED to:
 
 

1.             
Approve the establishment of a Joint Portfolio with
Gloucestershire’s District Councils to deliver Local
Government Reorganisation in Gloucestershire and establish Joint
Governance arrangements for the Portfolio
 

2.             
Approve a contribution of £10.186 million to a
pooled budget established to support delivery of the
programme
 

3.             
Note a further contribution will be required to the
pooled budget once funding has been agreed
 

4.             
Agree to accept a contribution from each District
Council into that pooled budget and for the County Council to act
as its Accountable Body, discharging responsibility for the
programme
 

5.             
Delegate authority to the Chief Executive, in
consultation with the Leader of the Council to agree and enter into
a Memorandum of Understanding with the six District Councils that
will set out how the Joint Programme is to be governed and
overseen
 

6.            
Delegate authority to the Deputy Chief
Executive/Executive Director of Corporate Resources and to the
Local Government Reorganisation Portfolio Director to authorise
expenditure from the pooled budget, in accordance with the
governance requirements set out in the Memorandum of Understanding,
providing that no single item of expenditure exceeds £500k.
Any decision that commits expenditure exceeding £500k will be
in accordance with the governance requirements set out in the
Memorandum of Understanding but will ultimately be referred to
Cabinet or the Leader of the Council to be taken as a key
decision.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to establish a joint programme with Gloucestershire's District Councils to deliver Local Government Reorganisation in Gloucestershire.

purpose:
Cabinet will be asked to approve the
distribution and use of the Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) for
2026/27.

The council receives an annual grant from the Department for
Education to fund the delivery of:
• Mainstream Primary and Secondary School Education.
• Early Years entitlements for 9 months, 2-year-olds and
3–4 year-olds.
• Central Services to support the delivery of local authority
statutory responsibilities for the local education system
• Delivery of services and support for children and young
people with SEND and additional education needs.

In 2025/26 the DSG provided to deliver these services totalled
£724.578m.

Consultation will be undertaken with the local Schools Forum ahead
of proposals to Cabinet to ensure the education system has been
consulted on key decisions relating to the distribution of
funding.

approval for the distribution and use of the Dedicated Schools
Grant (DSG) for 2026/27.
 
Having considered all of the
information, Cabinet noted the report and
 
RESOLVED to:
 
Subject to approval of the final
Council budget on the 18th February 2026, Cabinet approve use of
the Dedicated Schools Grant in 2026-27 as follows:

Schools
Block

That the Council agree the school
funding formula for 2026/27 be delivered based on a 0.0978%
reduction to the National Funding Formula rates, as set out in
Annex A. This is in line with Schools Forum’s agreement at
5th December Forum meeting, that any shortfall in the funding
needed, would be covered by reducing all NFF factor rates (except
the minimum per pupil levels) by the same percentage.
 
Central
School Services Block
To agree the use of the Central
School Services Block, as set out in paragraph 17,
fig.2.
 
High
Needs Block
Maintain funding in line with the
current forecast plan, which includes:
 

·      
A 3% uplift in EHCP top-up funding
 

·      
A targeted SEND funding budget of £3.2m to
support schools with significant numbers of children with
SEND.
 

·      
Not to undertake a 0.5% transfer from the schools
block
 
Early
Years Block
 
That cabinet agree to deliver the
Early Years rates, at the levels set out by the Departments for
Education and that Early Years providers are consulted on the
distribution of funding across the hourly rates, as set out in
fig.6 of this report and the majority decision is approved by the
Director of Childrens Services and
implemented.
 
That the full 3% allowed in the
funding guidance is retained and used as detailed in the
report.

purpose:
Both the adults and
young carers contracts are currently due to expire on 31 March
2026.  In March 2025 Cabinet approved the following: -
1.    
Cabinet approval was given to go out to tender for 2 Lots, Adult
and Young Carers.
2.    
Cabinet approval was given for a contract length of five years
with an option to extend for up to two years.
Following the
publication of the CQC report, a review of the adults service for
carers was undertaken to ensure they receive a robust offer.
As a result of the
review, this report sets out proposals to extend the current
contracts for Adult and Young Unpaid Carers support services in
Gloucestershire and proposed recommissioning of Adult Unpaid Carers
services. The approach for adults is aligned with the GCC Care
Quality Commission (CQC) Improvement Plan and the Adult Social Care
(ASC) Target Operating Model (TOM) to enable us to deliver
integrated, preventative, and outcome-focused services that
strengthens support for unpaid carers and ensure statutory
compliance.
The proposed model
will introduce a single contract for core carers’ services
and transfer Carers Emergency Scheme (CES) and Carers Breaks
packages to external providers under the existing GCC Health and
Social Care Framework. This strategic approach will enable us to
better meet the needs of unpaid carers now and into the future by
improving flexibility, simplifying processes, strengthening crisis
support, and enhancing carers’ resilience and wellbeing while
preventing service disruption.
This report seeks
Cabinet approval to:
·      
Extend the current contracts for adults and young carers by six
months.
·      
Delay and revise by six months the procurement of support for
adult carers.
·      
Agree the model for adult carers support.
 
The new adults contract will
commence on 1st October 2026.
 
Children’s
Services will commission the Young Carers contract as a separate
arrangement to ensure continuity of support and prevent any gaps in
provision. This approach allows for a more focused and targeted
tender process, tailored specifically to the needs of young carers.
This report will be presented to Cabinet in early 2026, with the
intention to go out to tender in April/May 2026.

intention to go out to tender in April/May 2026.
 

Cllr Kate Usmar and Cllr Ben Evans sought Cabinet approval
to:


·               
Extend the current contracts for adults and young
carers by six months.

·               
Delay and revise by six months the procurement of
support for adult carers.

·               
Agree the model for adult carers support.
 
 
Having considered all of the
information, Cabinet noted the report and
 
RESOLVED to:
 

1.   
Approve the following model for the future provision of
carers’ support services:


·      
Single contract for adult carers: A single contract will be
tendered for core adult carers’ services, with the overall
value adjusted to reflect the changes below.


·      
Carers Emergency Scheme (CES): GCC will source emergency care
packages through the existing Health and Social Care (H&SC)
Framework. When a carer faces an emergency and no one else can
help, a registered domiciliary care provider will deliver a
pre-agreed support package to the cared-for person.


·      
Carers Breaks: GCC will arrange carers’ breaks using
providers from the H&SC Framework via Adult Social Care
brokerage, which will source and coordinate appropriate
providers.


·      
Young Carers: a separate contract subject to Cabinet approval of
the procurement approach in March.


·      
Approve postponing the start of new contracts for adult and young
carers to allow time to implement this revised approach.

2. Extends existing
contracts with PeoplePlus Group Limited
(adult carers) and Gloucestershire Young Carers (young carers) by
way of contract modifications for six months from 1 April 2026 to
30 September 2026.

3.Delegate authority
to the Executive Director of Adult Social Care, Wellbeing and
Communities, in consultation with the Cabinet Member
for Adults’ Support & Independence, to:
 
 
·      
Run a competitive procurement process for
adult carers’ support (as outlined above), with a contract
term of 5 years plus an option to extend for up to 2
years.
·      
Award the contract to the preferred
bidder.
·      
Decide whether to exercise the extension
option at the end of the initial term.

content:
To seek Cabinet approval to procure three new
framework agreements under which Gloucestershire County Council
(GCC) may call-off statutory servicing works; minor responsive and
reactive works; and medium size project work respectively.

Cllr Colin Hay sought Cabinet
approval to procure three new framework agreements under which
Gloucestershire County Council (GCC) may call-off statutory
servicing works; minor responsive and reactive works; and medium
size project work respectively.
 
 
Having considered all of the information,
Cabinet noted the report and
 
RESOLVED to:
 
Delegate authority to the
Assistant Director - Asset Management and Property Services (AMPS),
in consultation with the Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for
Finance, Assets and Transformation to:


1.             
Conduct a competitive procurement process in respect
of the following new four-year multi-supplier framework
agreements:
 
(a) A framework agreement under
which GCC, certain schools, academies, NHS bodies, and district and
borough councils in Gloucestershire may award call-off contracts
for the supply of statutory servicing, reactive and remedial
works where the annual value of any call-off contract for such
works shall not exceed £250,000;

(b) A framework agreement under
which GCC, certain schools, academies, NHS bodies, and district and
borough councils in Gloucestershire may award call-off contracts
for the supply of minor responsive and reactive works where
the annual value of any call-off contract for such works shall not
exceed £325,000;
 
(c) A framework agreement under
which GCC, certain schools, academies, NHS bodies, and district and
borough councils in Gloucestershire may award call-off contracts
for the supply of medium size capital maintenance and
project works where the annual value of any call-off contract
for such works shall be between £15,000 and
£150,000.
 
 

2.             
Appoint each of the preferred tenderers to the
appropriate Lot under the above Framework Agreements.
 

3.             
Procure and award as many call-off contracts under
the above Framework Agreements as may be required by GCC for the

content:
Cllr Colin Hay sought Cabinet approval for the development of the Coombe Hill site to include
a new Fire and Rescue Service training facility, highways depot,
care home, and residential housing.
 
Having considered all of the
information, Cabinet noted the report and
 
RESOLVED
to:
 
(a)Approve the return of 27 acres
of GCC-owned land from the current farm tenant at Coombe Hill
adjacent to the A4019 to the County Council.

(b)Approve (subject to planning
permission) for the development of the land for use as a Fire
Training Centre, Highways Depot, Care Home and Housing Development
(of approx. 25 homes). Appendix 4 provides a location plan showing
location and red line for the development land.

(c)Approve submission of a
planning application for the development then, subject to approval
of that application, commits up to £46.7 million of capital
investment to build a new Fire and Rescue Training Centre, Highways
Depot and Care Home and for the enhancement of five satellite Fire
Stations.

(d) Approve the re-allocation of
£3 million capital expenditure budget within the total
£46.7 million, which was originally allocated to cover the
cost of purchasing land for the Care Home, to be used as an overall
project contingency fund.
 
(e) Delegate authority to the
Assistant Director of Asset Management and Property Services, in
consultation with the Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Finance,
Assets & Transformation to:
 

i.              
Appoint professional construction
services, who will manage the procurement and delivery of the
project.


ii.             
Negotiate the surrender of the land
from the tenant and agree appropriate compensation. If this is not
possible, to serve notice under the agricultural
tenancy/agricultural holding and, where appropriate, to pay
statutory compensation.


iii.            
Conduct a mini competition process,
that adheres with conditions under the Framework Agreement;
Contractor Partnering Framework Agreement: Major Construction Works
2024.


iv.           
Upon conclusion of the mini
competition, to enter into the above-mentioned pre-construction
design and, one or more contracts for the construction works with
the preferred contractor(s) evaluated as offering the Council best
value for money.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the development of the Coombe Hill site for a new Fire and Rescue Service training facility, highways depot, care home, and housing development.

purpose:
To approve Strategic Economic Devlopment Fund
(SEDF) funding for a number of bids/projects submitted for
consideration by the City Region Board
content:
Having considered all the information, the
Board noted the Officer’s recommendations and took account of
the funding which is currently allocated to the Strategic Economic
Development Fund (SEDF) and
 
RESOLVED to:
 
Allocate funding from the Strategic Economic
Development Fund (SEDF) to support the below projects which
contribute to the economic growth agenda and delivery of the
priorities of the City Region Board, including contributing to
sustainable growth, inward investment, contribute to the employment
and skills agenda and provide support to Gloucestershire
businesses.
 
The bids have been agreed in principle subject
to the City Region Board’s Senior Officer Group agreeing the
individual performance framework and expected outcomes for each
project.
 
 
SEDF Bid 1:
Gloucestershire Local Area Energy Plan and Energy Officer
 
The Board noted that this bid had particular strengths, which aimed to fund the
production of an Energy Plan and recruitment of an Energy Officer
to support the energy resource planning and oversee production of a
clear Energy Plan for the county, setting priorities and providing
strong evidence on future demand, generation, and infrastructure.
It positions Gloucestershire alongside other authorities and
ensures we can contribute fully to the South
West Regional Energy Strategic Planning (RESP) Transitional
Plan and the enduring RESP plan. The project builds lasting
capacity through officer training and expertise, supports a formal
RESP submission in 2026, and includes early work on cost
efficiencies and commissioning which makes it a strategic
investment with long-term benefits.
 
Funding amount requested: £325,000
Decision: to award
funding for the full amount requested: £325,000.
 
 
SEDF Bid 2:
Gloucestershire Careers Hub
 
The Board noted that the Gloucestershire
Careers Hub asked for £596,299 in funding over 3.5 years. The
project focused on improving and enhancing the current careers
education in schools and colleges, while helping employers promote
their brand awareness and job opportunities to students and
teachers. Its aim was to inspire young people to think about future
careers and aligns with the region’s economic priorities of
sustainable growth, inward investment, employment and skills, and
business support.

This funding would allow the Hub to access an annual grant from the
Department for Education via the Careers & Enterprise Company,
which provides 50% match funding for the staff delivery team as
well as local delivery fund for the project and a fully funded
project leader. It would also expand the Hub’s work to
include resources for key growth sectors such as green skills,
cyber, and digital. The project will increase its reach to 62
schools and colleges and grow its network of more than 100
employers.
 
Funding amount requested: £596299
Decision: to award the funding amount of £392,000 over a
two-year funding period.
 
 
SEDF Bid 3: The
Growth & Enterprise Team at GCC – Inward Investment
support
 
The Board noted the project requested
£350,000 in funding (reduced from an original
£380,000). It aimed to strengthen Gloucestershire’s
ability to attract investment by increasing the capacity of the
current team, which is very small at just 1.2 FTE. With reduced
national and regional support, this funding would allow the team to
expand and compete for investment, noting that other local
authority areas have larger teams. It would enable Gloucestershire
to promote its assets more effectively at national and
international events, engage with intermediaries such as the
British Embassy network, and showcase opportunities and key assets
to attract foreign direct investment. The project would also
strengthen links with universities and colleges, aligning
investment with skills development and workforce
opportunities.

Funding amount requested: £350,000
Decision: to award
the full revised funding amount of £350,000
 
 
SEDF Bid 4: Growing
the Advanced Engineering and Manufacturing (AEM) Sector in
Tewkesbury Borough and Gloucestershire
 
The Board noted that this project was seeking
£400,000 which aimed to unlock the growth potential of
Gloucestershire’s Advanced Engineering & Manufacturing
(AEM) Sector, which is a major contributor to supporting the local
economy, and provides high quality jobs, as well as skills and
training opportunities for the local workforce. The funding would
support countywide initiatives, led by Tewkesbury Borough Council,
in partnership with all the other local authorities. Key actions
include deploying dedicated AEM advisors through the Growth Hub
network to assist SMEs with some of the barriers to growth such as
skills, innovation, access to finance and premises and establishing
an AEM business board/group to provide strategic industry
leadership. The business case was based on key findings from its
recent AEM study, and outcomes including over 150 businesses
supported, c170 jobs created/retained and estimated £3.5m GVA
uplift.
 
Funding amount requested: £400,000
Decision: to award
the full funding amount requested of £400,000
 
 
SEDF Bid 5:
Future-Proofing the Visitor Economy: A
Strategic Framework for Sustainable Growth in Gloucestershire and
the Cotswolds
 
The Board noted that this project was
requesting £300,000, and was a collaborative initiative led
by all seven local authority areas. It aimed to create a unified
county data platform for the tourism and visitor economy sector,
eliminating duplication and inconsistency. This platform would
provide real-time insights to support smarter planning, investment,
and marketing for both public and private sectors. It would
strengthen Gloucestershire’s position nationally, by having a
new countywide Strategic Visitor Economy Growth Plan, that would
align with Visit England’s new strategy and partnership
arrangements and enable access to future funding
opportunities.

The project would also directly help local businesses in the sector
to adapt to market trends, manage tourism capacity, and optimise
their operations. It would support sustainable growth and regional
competitiveness. Expected outcomes include visitor growth of
5–10% over the next three years, new visitor-related jobs,
and open access to research data for businesses and
stakeholders.
 
Funding amount requested: £300,000
Decision: To award
the full funding amount requested of £300,000.
 
 
Bid 6: Resilient
Futures Lab: Gloucestershire’s centre for energy management
and environmental monitoring
 
The Board noted Hartpury University was
requesting £395,000, to create a living lab environment that
tests a range of technologies including automation, AI, and
environmental sensors to optimise energy use, model clean energy
generation, and support biodiversity. The lab would also showcase
emerging agri-tech, precision farming,
and smartphone-based crop monitoring, while embedding green skills
into education and modelling climate resilience strategies. The
funding would enable Hartpury to accelerate the project.

The lab would deliver benefits including testing new technologies
in real-world live settings and providing green skills training to
1,000 students. Other outcomes include creating three jobs, hosting
workshops for 130 professionals, supporting five businesses to
improve energy efficiency, publishing five case studies, and
developing a business case to ensure the lab’s sustainability
beyond 2028.

Funding amount requested:
£395,000
Decision: To award
£133,000 of the requested £395,000
 
 
 
Bid 7: SIDEKICK
Venture Studio
 
The Board noted that the project had requested
£400,000 to establish Gloucestershire’s first dedicated
cyber, national security, and defence-focused venture studio. The
aim was to turn the region’s untapped potential into a
sustainable engine for technology businesses. The first portfolio
will create 30 high-growth start-ups over three years. Funding
would provide specialist operational resources such as legal,
marketing, and technical support to reduce risks for early-stage
ventures and accelerate their time to market.

This very innovative project complements existing regional
initiatives and strengthens the significant cyber and digital
ecosystem. Expected outcomes include creation of over 300
high-value jobs across Gloucestershire, in cyber, defence and
national security. The roles would span product development,
engineering, operations, marketing and executive leadership across
the cohort of high growth start-ups. This growth will generate
£31.5 million in GVA and boosting the regional supply chain.
It would also encourage students to apply to local universities and
support, as well as benefitting local training/apprenticeship
providers, and any local entrepreneurs who might be seek new
careers pathways.

Funding amount
requested: £400,000
Decision: To award
the funding amount of £300,000 (as an investment loan)

Cllr Paul Hodgkinson sought delegated
authority to procure a Framework Agreement and call-off of
contracts under it. These relate to the provision of behaviour
change interventions for perpetrators of domestic abuse, i.e. the
service known as Positive Relationships Gloucestershire (PRG).
 
Having considered all of the information,
Cabinet noted the report and
 
RESOLVED to:
 
Delegate authority to the Director of Public
Health, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Public Health,
Communities and Fire to:
 
1. Conduct a competitive procurement process
in respect of a four-year single provider Framework Agreement for
the supply of the council’s Positive Relationships
Gloucestershire service. The Framework Agreement shall be awarded
to one provider who will deliver services under the following
Lots:
 

·      
Lot A: Core service delivery, perpetrator behaviour change and
early response interventions.


·      
Lot B: Local delivery of the ‘Drive Project’.

·      
Lot C: Provision of specialist perpetrator training for
professionals.
 
2. Appoint the preferred sole tenderer to this
single provider Framework Agreement.
 
3. Award a call-off contract for the supply of
the core service and intervention delivery under Lot A to the sole
appointed supplier under the above Framework Agreement. The
proposed call-off contract will continue for an initial period of
four years and include an option to extend its term for a further
period of two years on its fourth anniversary (i.e., four + two
years), a separate Cabinet decision shall be sought to authorise
the taking up of this extension. This call-off will include a break
clause on its second anniversary.
 
4. Award, subject to the financial limit set
out in the Resource Implications section of this Report below and
any subsequent funding allocations, as many call-off contracts as
may be required by the council under Lots A - C of the Framework
Agreement and to also exercise any extension options under them. If
the value of any individual proposed call-off contract exceeds
£500,000, a separate key decision shall be sought to
authorise this.

Gloucestershire Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner (OPCC)
under which the council will receive a funding transfer from
Gloucestershire OPCC for the purpose of part-funding (i.e., 30%) of
the cost of the call-off contract described in Recommendation 3 (on
the basis described in paragraph 15 of this report).
 
6. Enter into a s256 agreement with the
Gloucestershire Integrated Care Board (ICB) under which the council
will receive a funding transfer from the ICB for the purposes of
part-funding (i.e., 18%) the cost of the call-off contract
described in Recommendation 3 (on the basis described in paragraph
15 of this report).

content:
The National Landscape Conservation Board for
the Malvern Hills has requested that GCC adopt its Management Plan.
The Conservation Board for the Cotswolds National Management Plan
has asked that GCC endorse its Management Plan.
 
The Malvern Hills National Landscape
Management Plan 2025-30 and the Cotswolds National Landscape
Management Plan 2025-30 are statutory plans. They set out the
vision, outcomes and policies for the management of these areas for
the period 2025-2030. GCC, as a ‘relevant authority’
under the CROW Act, has a duty to consider the potential effect any
of its decisions and activities will have on the National
Landscape.
 

Cllr Julian Tooke, Cabinet Member: Business,
Economic Development, Planning and Infrasture approved the following decision in
relation to Adoption of the Malvern Hills National Landscape
Management Plan 2025-30 and endorsement of the Cotswolds National
Landscape Management Plan 2025-30
 
In coming to this
decision, Cllr Tooke gave due and full regard to the requirements
of the public sector equality duty contained in section 149 of the
Equality Act 2010 (“the Act”) by reference to the law
itself.
 
Having fully
considered all the available information, Cllr Tooke decided to
reject the alternative options and take the recommended decisions
to:
 
a)            
Adopt the Malvern Hills National Landscape Management Plan
2025-30
 
b)            
Endorse the Cotswolds National Landscape Management Plan
2025-30
 
For the reasons set
out in the published decision report.

decision_maker: Executive Director of Adult Services, Wellbeing and Communities
purpose:
Following a competitive process initially
intended to establish a Framework Agreement for the delivery of
residential and nursing care services, and in consultation with for
Cabinet Member for Adults’ Support and Independence, in
accordance with the Cabinet decision of 15 May 2024, the Council
has since revised its approach.



While the original intention was to use a Framework Agreement, we
have subsequently decided to proceed with a Master Services
Agreement (MSA) instead. This change is based on external legal
advice and reflects a more appropriate contractual model for the
nature of the services being commissioned. This adjustment ensures
contractual clarity and better alignment with the Council’s
commissioning intentions, without altering the substance of the
original decision.



DECISION

To award a Contract for the supply of residential and nursing care
services within five care homes in the Council’s estate to
Agincare Homes Holdings Ltd. The Contract will be for an initial
period of five years.



Subject to mutual agreement between the Council and the provider,
and further Cabinet approvals, the Contract may be extended for
additional periods of up to five years, provided that the final
expiry date does not exceed 31 January 2040.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member - Nature, Climate & Waste Reduction
purpose:
To authorise preparatory work in support of
the refurbishment of Household recycling Centres, including the
vital improvement works at Hempstead and the appointment of a
contractor from the Gloucestershire County Council Major
Contractors Framework for all capital works in excess of
£150k

To authorise a procurement exercise to determine the supplier for
static waste compaction equipment to be supplied and installed as
part of the Hempsted Household Recycling Centre refurbishment
works.
content:
That the Cabinet Member for
Nature, Climate and Waste Reduction rejects the alternative options
and takes the recommended decision to:
 
1.   
Delegate authority to the Assistant Director of
Asset Management & Property Services in consultation with the
Cabinet Members for Nature, Climate and Waste Reduction and the
Cabinet Member for Finance, Assets and Transformation to procure
and award a call-off contract under the Gloucestershire County
Council (GCC’s) “Major Contractors Framework for all
works in excess of £150k” for the supply of preparatory
design work, planning permission submissions and building works in
relation to vital improvement works at Hempsted HRC.
 
2.   
Delegate authority to the Executive Director of
Economy, Environment & Infrastructure in consultation with the
said Cabinet Member to progress the vital repair works through to
completion. This will include the closure of Hempsted HRC to the
public for approximately 2 months commencing in mid-January
2026.
 
3.   
Delegate authority to the Executive Director of
Economy, Environment & Infrastructure in consultation with Cllr
Martin Horwood, Cabinet lead for nature, climate and waste
reduction to:
 
a)   
Conduct a competitive procurement process in respect
of a contract for the supply, delivery, installation and ongoing
servicing and maintenance of static waste compaction equipment at
Hempsted HRC powered by 100% renewable electricity. The contract
shall also include an option, subject to available funding, to
supply similar waste compaction equipment and related services at
other council HRCs that will be the subject of separate Cabinet or
(as appropriate) Individual Cabinet Member decisions at the
relevant time. The term of the proposed contract shall be up to
five years.
b)   
Award the above supply, delivery, installation and
ongoing servicing contract to the preferred tenderer, which shall
make provision for a two-year fixed price for static waste
compaction equipment supplied within this period. Equipment ordered
after this period shall be evaluated by the Council for value for
money and prices negotiated with the contractor.
 
For the reasons set out in the
report.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Nature, Climate and Waste Reduction has decided to delegate authority for vital improvement works and waste compaction equipment procurement at Hempsted HRC.
